descriptionChirho: The proper noun Mikah (Micah), referring to several biblical persons including the Ephraimite of Judges 17-18, the prophet Micah of Moresheth, and others. All four clusters represent the same personal name with minor spelling variants and prepositional differences: the main form Mikhah (eng: Mikhah/Mikah, spa: Mica/Micaias, arb: مِيخَا/مِيكَا, kor: 미가, swa: Mika), a variant spelling Micah (eng: Micah, spa: Miqueas), the prepositional form to-Mikhah (eng: to-Mikhah, arb: لِ–مِيخَا), and a ketiv variant Mikhayehu (spa: Mijayehu, arb: ميكهو). Hindi consistently renders मीकाह/मीका across all forms.
